steps.content: I can't tell when exactly this started. But no matter how I fall asleep, the lessons from my childhood always appear at the beginning of my dreams...

steps.speaker: Old Professor
steps.content: Today, you will embark on your journey into the study of history. Before we begin, there is one thing I hope you will always remember...

steps.speaker: Old Professor
steps.content: As historians, we must face our own ignorance with honesty, and never let bias or sentiment cloud our judgment. We will always question our findings, always remain objective and independent, and pursue the truth at any cost.
My name is Celine Fabius. I am a Disian. When I was six years old, my family discovered that I possessed an extraordinary memory. I could memorize the contents of any book after just a single glance.
So, at a very young age, I entered my grandfather's private academy, studying alongside people many years my senior, all of us learning what it meant to become true scholars of history.
By modern medical standards, it would be considered a disorder. But for someone like me, someone who had always loved history, it felt less like an affliction and more like a calling.

steps.speaker: Older Student
steps.content: She can memorize anything after reading it just once... She doesn't even know half the words yet... So this is what they call a genius, huh... I'm so jealous... Why would someone like her choose such an unprofitable field of study...

steps.speaker: Mother
steps.content: If this is where your passion lies, then pursue it. It won't be an easy path, but you will become a remarkable historian. We will always be proud of you.
(Flashback to the ceremonial hall or the private school)
My grandfather had many students under his tutelage and nurtured countless accomplished scholars. I can still picture every one of their faces, even now. Well, it is my special gift, after all.
Lucie, Theodore, Davy, Sasham, Qiu Qiu, Morton, Pierce...

History flows like a river, forever rushing onward. In the fleeting span of a single lifetime, to seek the truth of this world is a great endeavor—a journey with no clear destination and no easy way home.

steps.speaker: Lucie
steps.content: I know the history of the farlands that I have compiled does not please the authorities. That is why I can no longer remain in DisCity, or these records will never see the light of day. Goodbye... I am returning to the farlands, and I will find my own way to continue chronicling history!

steps.speaker: Theodore
steps.content: I passed the civil service exam for the Public Security Bureau. Turns out knowing DisCity's local customs inside and out actually comes in handy. Maybe I'll work my way up the ranks someday, who knows. Wish me a happy graduation, genius...

steps.speaker: Davy
steps.content: All our works can be destroyed in an instant. Not only by disasters, but by human hands. If humanity is so willfully blind, why should we continue striving to preserve these records?

The next time Lucie's name appeared, she had already been officially labeled a "terrorist." She often ventured deep into the disaster zones of the farlands in search of firsthand historical records, living among the contamination and Corruptors.

Theodore joined the Department of Communications and married a beautiful woman. After rising through the ranks of society, he advocated for a public data censorship bill, turning against his former colleagues.

As for Davy, he lost both legs during an operation in DisSea, but fortunately survived. In the end, he found his way back to the library, where he worked as a chronicler while quietly searching for the true meaning of history.

One by one, they threw themselves into that great river. Before I knew it, I was the only one left where I had begun. I was an observer who never waded into its waters, merely watching and recording it all.
And so, the names in her memory grow ever more numerous, and ever more vivid.
Those who record their own distorted version of history...

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: Biographical research is my specialty. I know of countless people like that... It's what I've dedicated my life to studying! So many people are forgotten simply because their stories aren't exciting enough, or because of their flaws. They're too ordinary to be seen as heroes, so no one wants to talk about them!

steps.speaker: Morton
steps.content: All I needed... was one opportunity to bring Glorie's history to light. People would remember these stories, this town, and those nameless heroes...
Those who scorn history, yet go on to make it...

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: He said that as long as people's lives improved, he didn't care if his name was erased from the library's records. He believed the welfare of the living was far more important than lifeless knowledge preserved on paper.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: His reputation was utterly ruined. His name was removed from every work he had authored, and he vanished completely from academia. But the people he had helped never forgot him. He remained in history in another form.
Those who cherish history, yet never hesitate to use it to their advantage...

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: These are authentic records from the early Black Ring operations. They contain experimental logs and research data on Mania patients from that era. These documents are priceless materials that have never been revealed to the public.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: With your expertise, I have no doubt you could craft a research report that would shake the entire academic world. And of course, you would receive full credit for it.
Those who call themselves observers of history, yet still find themselves swept up in it...
<size=42><color=#7683a2>[Ongoing Request] Reward Offered: N.F. 101 DisCity Prison Inmate Registry | Nirvana Port Surveillance Footage | Authentic Historical Records</size></color>

<color=#7683a2>Thousandhand_marf</color>: Got a chronological surveillance recording from the port depot. Also have a digitized smuggling ledger from August N.F. 101. Certified scans. What's your offer?

<color=#7683a2>Keluge</color>: My grandma left me a stack of letters from her old army buddies. All from before N.F. 100. Will you pay for these? Look, there are tons of them. [Image][Image][Image]

<color=#7683a2>Nailwind</color>: Everything you're looking for is restricted data, you know. My dad works at Nirvana. I can plant a virus on his device and sneak it all out for you.

<color=#fb9259>codename_ce</color>: I don't accept tampered footage or recompressed files. Scanned copies are worth less too. DM me.

<color=#7683a2>Mamaguagua</color>: Found the registry you want. The person you're looking for did enter the prison during N.F. 101 and got exiled in N.F. 102. The prison was demolished by the end of that year.

<color=#fb9259>codename_ce</color>: Did they leave behind any notebooks or diaries?

<color=#7683a2>Mamaguagua</color>: No chance. Even if they did, anything like that would've been destroyed the moment it was discovered. But I dug deeper, and the chronicler in charge of the prison records at the time was Harden Pierce. He died of a heart attack two years ago. His grandson inherited everything.

<color=#7683a2>Mamaguagua</color>: Total trust fund brat. Squanders his father's money throwing banquets and parties, trying to buy his way into Eastside's upper circles. Nobody's really interested, though. The Pierce family never had the kind of old-money pedigree that crowd actually cares about.

<color=#fb9259>codename_ce</color>: Thank you. Your information has been valuable. Payment will be transferred to your account within 8 hours.

<color=#fb9259>codename_ce</color>: Have a nice day.

The dark web is a remarkably useful tool. It offers access to all kinds of information unobtainable through legitimate channels. It is almost ironic that the most unfiltered truths reside in the darkest corners of the internet.
Celine's gaze drifts slowly down the screen, the scattered threads of the story weaving together in her mind.
[The Truth Behind the Battle of the Rust][Maris Andre Memorial Hall Opens Soon: Rare Historical Documents on Display for the First Time!][Could Maris Andre's True Family Name Be Pierce?]

The scheme is so shallow and flimsy that it's almost laughable. Its influence is far too limited to draw in enough important figures. In that case, why not add a little fuel to the fire and turn it into a major scandal?
In the climate-controlled vault, Chief and Pierce exchange pleasantries in the background as she drifts closer to the carefully preserved collection.
Behind the familiar strokes and sharp writing on the page, their faces emerge from the depths of an unforgettable sea of memories.
Humanity continues to repeat the same history, making the same mistakes again and again. Civilization is a glorious yet fragile thing, one that can collapse in an instant.
If destruction is inevitable, then what is the point of continuing to record all this?
And yet...
We ask you that remember us.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I will, my dear friends. I'm here to bring you home.

A few days later, the forgery case surrounding Maris Andre is finally exposed. The Public Security Bureau launches a crackdown on several illegal media outlets, and the investigation even uncovers leads pointing to Outland spies and an intelligence smuggling operation. The 9th Agency is currently celebrating their good fortune, reaping the rewards without lifting a finger.
It is around this time that you hear of Celine's discharge from the hospital and receive an enormous parcel from the Central Library.
"Thank you for your assistance during this operation, Chief. Enclosed is the highest-level access I can grant. The doors of the Central Library are always open to you."

This is your first visit to the Central Library. Nestled within a secluded garden with United University behind it, it stands across from the Ring Research Institute, yet the two are worlds apart in terms of size and public attention.

You take the elevator to the heart of the library. Shelves rise all the way to the ceiling, arranged in chronological order and stretching on like an endless scroll. Hovering rails connect them, while dim light falls across the uneven spines, revealing gaps where volumes once stood.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The modernization of the DisCity Army... Escalating political and military tensions... Border budget in crisis... Refugee influx from WhiteSands doubles in the same year...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Nirvana's unmanned mining project... Bid evaluation records... EDGE external summit minutes...

These sensitive documents sit openly on the shelves like bestsellers. Yet you feel like a parched man cast into the ocean, or a blind man standing beneath the blazing sun. As a layperson, you simply cannot find what you seek in this vast sea of information.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Even with access, I can't make sense of the system. If I want to borrow anything, I'll still need her help... How cunning.
The deeper you go, the more towering the shelves become. Rounding a corner, you spot a familiar figure.

She is perched on a lift chair, sorting through some documents, hovering around the N.F. 115 section. From a distance, she looks like a pink bookmark about to be swallowed by the vast sea of files. Only when she spots you does she slowly drift back down.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Welcome to the library, Chief ${PlayerName}. You must have received my gift.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes, nearly two hundred books, including the A Brief History of DisCity series, bestsellers, popular novels, science primers... Our little library's collection has grown by more than half. The kids all love them.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And this is my first time venturing this deep into the Central Library and seeing the archives for myself. It's truly impressive. Though I can't help but wonder what methods were used to gather all of this.
You study her face, still as gentle as ever, and begin laying out the information you have obtained over the past few days.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We were only investigating the forgery case concerning Maris Andre at first, which was supposed to be nothing more than a minor public order violation. Yet we ended up drawing out the Pierce family and even Outland spies.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The 9th Agency walked away with a huge prize, and every other department got something out of it as well. But if you ask me who came out on top, it was the Central Library. You ended up acquiring a substantial portion of the Pierce family's collection for free.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Quite a few talented individuals from the Pierce family have served this library. As Head Librarian of the Central Library, I will never forget the considerable contributions made by these collectors.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Never forget their contributions, huh... That's a lovely way to put it.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The Maris Andre forgery case is a scandal to the public, a lead for the Public Security Bureau, and a windfall for the 9th Agency. But to you, it is the perfect pretext.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: With that pretext in hand, you could apply for a special warrant and have the entire Pierce estate collection seized, including any potential forgeries. The Public Security Bureau is busy with its investigation, the media is having a field day on the front pages, and here you are, sitting quietly in the library, waiting for everything you've been searching for to be delivered straight to your door.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Did you have fun setting up the trap, Professor Celine?
Celine's smile fades, but her gaze remains gentle. Perhaps it is just your imagination, but she seems to be reading something in you, tracing every detail with her eyes, committing it all to memory.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: They all say the MBCC's Chief is exceptionally intelligent. I suspect there is more to your reasoning. Can I hear the rest?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's all I have. The rest is just speculation.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You were looking for the manuscripts the Pierce family had kept hidden, while my attention was drawn to the shady dealings behind the wave of "debunking" stories. And how fortunate we were to have the renowned Head Librarian volunteer as an expert advisor. Now that it's all over, I suppose I owe the library a favor.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: As for whether you've had any covert dealings with the 9th Agency, my guess is... not yet. But the windfall you brought them could very well lead to a new connection. Am I right?
You pause for a moment.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: There's another thing... You've mentioned the lack of funding and dwindling visitors a few times, but the Central Library is, in fact, an important facility under Paradeisos. Surely you have students, colleagues, and other connections you could rely on as well. Why did you decide to handle the Maris Andre case personally?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What's hidden in those manuscripts from the Pierce collection that made you so eager to obtain them? And why did it have to be <color=#fb9259>you</color> who acquired them?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Smart, honorable, highly perceptive... I just wonder whether a mind like that can remain unchanged...

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: ...Fine. I owe you an apology. Please forgive me for approaching you the way I did. I tried to make it up to you by granting you a rather high level of access.
She holds her faint smile and extends a hand in invitation.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: It's your first time here, Chief. Let me show you around while I offer you my explanation.
You step onto the hovering device and let it carry you to the shelves. You watch as she pulls out a red-covered book and opens it.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: This is the Nightfall Chronicle, a detailed account of the upheaval that swept through human society in the early years after Nightfall. It documents everything from daily life to the collective mindset of society at the time. It is an extraordinarily valuable historical record. Its author, Barney, lived through the N.F. 20s. He was already in his sixties when the Perishing Star fell, yet he still traveled across multiple cities, leaving behind millions of words of documentation.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Transportation was largely paralyzed back then, and contamination was spreading across the land. But the hardships never slowed him down—not until Mania claimed him and his wife in their sleep, turning them into Corruptors. After his death, much of his work was destroyed as hazardous material. Barely 10% of his records have been salvaged.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: To recover this remaining fragment, Lucie dug through five graveyards. She was exposed to too much contamination in the process, and passed away not long after.
You've seen this document in Morton's photocopy. But this is the first time you've heard of Lucie, the name of the chronicler.
The book retriever drifts slowly along the shelves. Further ahead, Celine draws out another book, this one with a black cover.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: After the N.F. 30s, DisCity developed rapidly under the colonization of the metropoles and entered a golden age. This journal meticulously documents the daily lives of Syndican miners.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: But it wasn't recovered until the late N.F. 90s. Filled with verifiable facts and supported by documented accounts of Nirvana's exploitation of its workers, it circulated widely through Syndicate for a time, only to be swiftly branded a "collection of lies," banned, and destroyed.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Theodore spent five months digging through government databases before finally identifying his name. He was called Ramboll Wade, a cobbler who was so insignificant, yet so influential.
She pauses for a moment, clutching the book to her chest. The book retriever carries you both onward to the next shelf.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: This one was compiled by Davy Buerz and contains records about the Pioneer unit of the Ring Research Institute. From the N.F. 80s onward, the abilities of Sinners gradually became known to the public, and among some of them, a brief yet fervent worship of Mania, and even the Black Ring, took hold.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: The Pioneer unit ventured into the unstable parameters of the contamination zones, carrying an early model of the Hypercube shield, and documented the changes in various Black Ring indicators.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: According to their records, the changes in the Black Ring indicators formed distinct patterns that they could only describe as "moods," ones that even seemed to respond to human behavior. The discovery sent them into a frenzy. They classified it as a biological phenomenon rather than a purely physical one.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: We now know that Black Rings are not independent living beings. Much of the knowledge surrounding Black Rings has since become classified information. As for this book, which contained outdated methods, incorrect conclusions, and views contrary to accepted doctrine, it was banned shortly after its publication.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And the people involved...

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Most of them have passed away. Only Mr. Oliver is still alive, spending his remaining years as a long-term patient at Banyan Medical College. Alzheimer's has taken away most of his memories.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: The Ring Research Institute funded multiple editions, and after countless revisions, we were able to preserve a redacted version for internal use. We send Mr. Oliver the latest revision each time. What you're holding is the first edition, the one that was scheduled for recall and destruction.

She stands before the towering shelves and speaks of every book like an old friend, introducing you to each chronicler who brought these documents back. As she speaks, the unfamiliar names take shape, until they feel like people standing right in front of you.

The shelves stretch endlessly upward, with light and shadow shifting across them. The figures of these people emerge and fade among the rows of books, like leaves drifting along the great river of history.
Finally, she brings you to a pile of uncatalogued documents, and gestures toward the files just transferred from the Pierce estate.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: These were all recovered from the Pierce family collection. Generations ago, their ancestors were collaborators of the library who handled a considerable number of documents.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Documents deemed "incorrect," "dangerous," and marked for destruction.
Every era pursues its own version of the "truth." Harden Pierce understood this and did all he could to preserve the truths that could never be spoken aloud.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: That was why they preserved some of these truths and kept them hidden until now. They were all meticulous. They knew exactly what it would mean if any of it ever came to light. But the generation that inherited them used them to produce blatant forgeries for profit.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The humanities have been in decline for a long time now. Priceless collections lose their value the moment they're moved into the library.
A wry smile crosses her face. She lowers her eyes.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: The Pierce family itself has a rich history, yet its current head hasn't a shred of historical sensibility. Better it all pass into my hands than be squandered by someone like him.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I dislike conflict, but I refuse to watch my colleagues' life's work gather dust.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So you decided to take over the collection. Because you knew that if it remained in the hands of that wastrel, not only would the distorted history twist people's understanding of the past, but the sensitive documents his family had fought so hard to preserve would also be exposed, scrutinized, or even destroyed.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You want to protect these documents, but every manuscript and dataset here has a traceable code...
Unconsciously, your voice drops to a near whisper.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Is that why you came to me? Can I help?
She smiles, then extends her hand toward you.
A pulse of Mania spreads from her palm, and with it, the shackles take hold.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Chief, I didn't come this far alone. I have many friends, mentors, and students. Most of them have been far less fortunate than I am, yet they continue to walk this path all the same.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I was blessed with the gift of memory. The least I can do is put it to meaningful use.

She raises her hand like a seer performing a ritual, and the sheets of paper in the room all rise and swirl in orderly streams, sweeping past her eyes one by one. A hurricane suddenly erupts in this space where time has long stood still.

The pages let out a soft shriek as ink flows into them. Words and materials from different eras sweep past your eyes. History rearranges itself in a nonlinear order. Words are connected by nothing but logic.
Prayers whispered beneath the eclipsed moon, a land deed from the metropoles, a list of the deceased in WhiteSands, a secret military order from a forgotten era...
Every symbol breaks free from its cage, flowing joyfully into the river of history she commands, dissolving in it.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: They can destroy written records or grind stone carvings to dust, but they will never take what is etched in my mind.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Text can be lost or altered. But everything I have committed to memory has remained perfectly preserved.
Mania stirs your emotions through the shackles. You recall what she said in Pierce's study, that many of those manuscripts were painstakingly crafted by people she knew.
That is why she wants them. They are not merely a stack of records. They are proof that those people once lived.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Would that do?
She smiles and nods.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Thanks to your help, the library was able to recover so much invaluable data. <color=#fb9259>On my own</color>, I doubt I could have ever uncovered the conspiracy behind it all.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Save the flattery, Professor Celine. I'm already well aware that we're caught in the same web.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Next time you need help, just ask. No need to go through all that. I don't appreciate being manipulated... but I also can't leave you to do this alone.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Besides, you can tell me more about them, too. Not just what is written in the books, but who they actually were. I'd like to hear about that.
She chuckles and walks over to the documents about to be destroyed, running her fingers gently over them as though saying goodbye to some old friends.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: You know, sometimes I find myself wondering... Chief, what if one day, for some reason, I lost my memories?
Her tone remains as gentle and casual as ever, but her smile doesn't reach her eyes.
You take a deep breath.

options: That happens to be my specialty.
We'll go and find them back.

choices.text: That happens to be my specialty.
We'll go and find them back.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: As it happens, I lost my memories by accident as well. If that day ever comes, at least you'll have someone who understands what you're going through.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm no chronicler or scholar, so I can't help you preserve documents. But I am a Mania specialist, and your ability is fundamentally tied to Mania. As long as the shackles remain intact, I'll do everything in my power to preserve it.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If that day ever comes, we'll do what the chroniclers do. Piece the fragments of history back together.
I have encountered so many people in the river of history.

<color=#e5b2cc><i>Those who record their own distorted version of history...
Those who scorn history, yet go on to make it...<i></color>
Those who cherish history, yet never hesitate to use it to their advantage... Those who call themselves observers of history, yet still find themselves swept up in it...
And those who remember history... and continue to move forward...

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: ...Heh. Then... it's a promise.
